new_statements.quote: Unfortunately, the nature of the Rituale as a data source makes it difficult to know how stress assignment might have worked in Puquina. We might speculate that Oré would have added diacritics if the pattern deviated far from Spanish, and indeed, there are in fact a handful of intriguing such cases (e.g. <èſumaruchunch> ‘he was revived’ [T.04]). However, these are too infrequent and inconsistent to draw any conclusions from.
new_statements.citation: Emlen, Nicholas Q., Arjan Mossel, Simon van de Kerke & Willem F. H. Adelaar. 2024. Puquina. In Matthias Urban (ed.), The Oxford Guide to the Languages of the Central Andes, 335-391. Oxford: Oxford University Press. doi:10.1093/oso/9780198849926.003.0012
new_statements.locator: Sec. 12.3.3 'Syllable structure and root structure', p. 344 (PDF page 11 of the Groningen Pure deposit)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (58 pp., Groningen Pure deposit of the OUP publisher's PDF, fetched sources from core.ac.uk/download/; cover page gives DOI 10.1093/oso/9780198849926.003.0012, 'Publisher's PDF / Version of record'). extracted text of PDF page 11 (printed p. 344, running head 'emlen, mossel, van de kerke, adelaar', end of sec. 12.3.3 'Syllable structure and root structure', immediately before 12.3.4 'Major morphophonological processes') yields exactly: 'Unfortunately, the nature of the Rituale as a data source makes it difficult to know how stress assignment might have worked in Puquina. We might speculate that Oré would have added diacritics if the pattern deviated far from Spanish, and indeed, there…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No stress rule can be stated: Puquina is extinct and attested essentially only in Ore's 1607 Rituale, whose orthography marks no systematic accent; the handful of grave-accented spellings are too sparse and inconsistent to interpret. The authors' only (explicitly speculative) inference is that stress probably did not deviate strikingly from Spanish-like patterns, since Ore did not feel the need to mark it.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the isolated diacritic cases such as <èſumaruchunch> 'he was revived' [text T.04], which the authors decline to interpret.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns word-level stress assignment as recoverable from a single early-17th-century written corpus; no spoken data exist (language extinct since the early 19th century).
new_statements.identity_note: The statement covers Puquina as attested in Ore's 1607 Rituale (texts probably from the Lake Titicaca / Juli area); Emlen et al. treat internal variation in sec. 12.2 but the stress remark applies to the whole corpus. Not to be confused with Kallawaya (call1235), the mixed language that preserves Puquina lexicon with Quechua grammar and phonology, nor with Uru/Chipaya, which colonial sources sometimes also called 'Puquina'.
